newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank stocks dominate Templeton India Growth Fund.
newsitem.headline: Bank stocks dominate Templeton India Growth Fund.

text.p: Bank stocks top Templeton India Growth Fund, the mutual fund told investors on Wednesday.
Banks and financial institutions amounted to 9.34 percent share in the mutual fund's net assets as on March 31, 1997.
The list included Industrial Development Bank of India, ICICI, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Bank of Baroda and the State Bank of India.
The second largest investment (7.49 percent of net assets) was in shares of diversified conglomerates Larsen & Toubro Ltd, Indian Rayon & Industries and Grasim Industries Ltd, the report said.
Energy companies ranked third, constituting 6.81 percent of net assets, Templeton India Growth Fund said.
The fund invested in three energy firms -- Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd, Cochin Refineries and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd.

"As on March 31, 1997, the funds under management has grown from 500 million rupees to 874.8 million rupees and we have invested 502.2 million rupees representing 57.41 percent in equities," the report said.
Investments are spread over 36 companies, it said. Privately placed debentures made up 5.72 percent of net assets.
The net asset value (NAV) as on March 31, 1997 was 10.04 rupees. The NAV improved to 10.64 rupees as on April 21, 1997.
Templeton India Growth Fund is the maiden domestic fund launched by the Indian subsidiary of the U.S. mutual fund.
